text: Lesson 1 mentioned Kafka retains events for a configured retention period. This lesson is that configuration — two independent limits, time and size, whichever hits first triggers deletion.
log.retention.hours deletes data older than a set number of hours. log.retention.bytes deletes the oldest data once a partition exceeds a size limit. Either one can trigger deletion first.
Compacted topics are a genuinely different model — instead of eventually deleting everything, they keep the latest value for every key forever, cleaning up only the superseded older values.

Time-based retention answers how much history to keep. Size-based sets a hard ceiling on disk usage. Compaction answers a different question — what does the current state look like right now, per key.
Three genuinely different retention models, not three versions of one idea. Next up: ZooKeeper vs. KRaft — what holds a Kafka cluster's metadata together.
